sites.rationale: Device-provided display topology register (number of display ports). The driver never writes BAR0+0x122c, so a shadow-RAM read would return 0 and Control::start would silently fall back to 1 port. Value must come from the host side at read time.
Root page-table PFN computed by the guest from its own descriptor; plain store into the shared BAR0 page is authoritative.
FIFO PFN computed by the guest from its own IOMemoryDescriptor; plain store.
FIFO length taken from the guest descriptor via IOMemoryDescriptor vtable; plain store.
Constant FIFO start offset 0x1000; plain store.
FIFO enable bit. Plain store is enough: x86 TSO preserves the store order of PFN/length/start/enable into the shared page and the daemon applies them in polling order.

FIFO write cursor updated by the device as it consumes commands. writeFifo() polls it in a loop to find free space; a shadow-RAM copy is stale and can make the loop spin or overwrite unconsumed commands.

patch.stub_operation: %esi = apv_mmio_read(%rcx, 0x100c, 4) + %edx   (reproduces the addl inside the span)
patch.notes: Loop head: the site is the branch target of jb at __TEXT+0x2b8b; every iteration must re-dispatch (live cursor).

sites.rationale: FIFO doorbell / write index. Stores into shared RAM are ordered after the FIFO data stores; the daemon polls the doorbell and applies it.

First half of the version-negotiation handshake: the written request is immediately read back (0x2cdf) and the read-back value drives the retry loop. The write and read must be one atomic dispatch (versionPair) so the device sees the request before the reply is sampled.

patch.stub_operation: %r12d = apv_mmio_version_pair(%rdx, 0x1034, %ecx)   (write then read on one dispatch)
patch.notes: Span covers BOTH the 3-byte write and the 4-byte read-back (2cdc/2cdf).

sites.rationale: Fallback version force-write after negotiation gives up. It is a pure write with no read-back, so a plain store is fine for memory semantics. NOTE: if the bridge must fail closed when the daemon is unreachable, this site must be dispatched instead (it is the only place that can report a transport failure back to configureDevice).

sites.rationale: Fault status latched by the device; non-zero diverts the interrupt action block into AppleParavirtAccelerator::handleFaultInterrupt(). A shadow-RAM copy would always read 0 and GPU faults would never be recovered. The surrounding branch must be reproduced by the stub.

patch.notes: Span covers the compare AND the 2-byte conditional branch je. The stub must discard the return address pushed by the patched call and transfer control to one of the two original destinations (tail-jump): __TEXT+0x2f26 (fault present, falls into handleFaultInterrupt) or __TEXT+0x2f32 (no fault).

sites.base_register: %rax (IOPCIDevice vtable pointer, NOT a BAR pointer)
sites.rationale: callq *0x8e0(%rax) where %rax is the IOPCIDevice vtable loaded from 0xdd8(%rbx). This is the vtable slot for the PCI capability lookup (argument %esi=5, i.e. MSI capability). It is NOT a BAR0 access and must not be patched.

FIFO disable on teardown. Ordering is load-bearing: the very next actions release the FIFO IOMemoryDescriptor/map and the BAR mapping, so the daemon must have applied (and acknowledged) the disable before teardown frees the pages. A plain RAM store gives no completion guarantee.

patch.stub_operation: apv_mmio_write_sync(%rax, 0x1000, 0, 4)   (must not return until the daemon acknowledged the disable)
patch.notes: Synchronous dispatch is required so the FIFO is quiesced before the descriptor/map are freed.

sites.rationale: Framebuffer start-up write to BAR0+0x1200. Pure write, no read-back; the daemon applies it while polling.
